evidence: Independently compared all six uses with the section 4 table across .github/workflows/ci.yml, evidence.yml and release.yml. GitHub REST public repository owner.login was actions and GET /repos/actions/{name}/commits/{release-tag} resolved to the listed 40-hex SHA for all six. https://github.com/actions

CI push, pull_request and reusable tests have contents:read. Dispatch-only evidence adds actions:read to fetch cross-run receipts. All checkouts disable persisted credentials. Ordinary release jobs use read scopes. Only release.attest requests OIDC and attestation writes; only release.publish requests contents:write, downstream of acceptance. Reviewed job steps, effective scopes and artifact destinations.
Every checkout in CI, evidence and release sets persist-credentials:false. Read permits fetch. The two jobs with write permissions use them for provenance and release publication respectively.
Used in CI tests, evidence preparation and read-only release verification; no packaging credentials or publishing permissions were supplied to setup-python.
Only ci.candidate and ci.jest set up Node to build/test the shell, both with contents:read.

Uploads to named same-run artifacts via Actions artifact service. CI uploads use contents:read; cross-run evidence has contents/actions reads. No extra repository write permission is granted for uploads. release.attest uses its job-level writes to create attestations.

CI and release reconstruct known named/patterned artifacts. Cross-run downloads of named-release-evidence in verify-release and accept-release use actions:read. No PAT supplied. publish downloads gated assets from its own run.

Only release.attest runs this action. It receives each verified pre-frozen file under build/candidate; contents:read, id-token:write and attestations:write are job-scoped. No contents write, registry login, or package push.
